mechanism: One payloaded aircraft suffers an observed critical system failure before successful mission completion; paired ordinary SERVICE versus built-in UNLOADING post-mission turnround tests positive unloading work after failure.

configuration.system_failure: FRT=300000 per million OPHOURS, RSEED=1, half-hour local direct repair, matching D01
configuration.turnround: ordinary SERVICE ten-minute control versus predefined <UNLOADING> ten-minute child

hypotheses_to_test: Both variants perform PAYLOADING before the 8-hour mission and observe an in-mission critical system failure before mission success.
The failed mission returns the aircraft; built-in UNLOADING performs positive ten-minute work rather than skipping, under the same failure timing as the ordinary SERVICE control.
Direct repair and turnround order, readiness, mission result, 72 half-hour report bins and terminal state reconcile without inferring payload quantity.
All populated source tables roundtrip exactly, conversion errors are zero, raw artifacts are sealed, and GUI/mutex guards hold.
limits: One fixed-seed failure and one payloaded mission only; other failure times and mission outcomes are unverified.
Internal payload quantity/state and fuel use are not directly measured.
Resource contention, GUI-only behavior and cross-engine parity remain unverified.
